options.metric: Police-reported crash count and percentage of all crashes
options.denominator: All crashes with crash_date from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (2,132,218 records)
options.grouping: Day of week across the full period
options.reason: The pooled counts and shares provide a direct summary of how recorded crashes were distributed among weekdays.
options.answer: Friday had the most crashes (338,800; 15.9% of the total), while Sunday had the fewest (257,544; 12.1%).
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the recorded crashes were divided among weekdays over the full period: Friday has the largest share and Sunday the smallest. It is a defensible pooled distribution of crash records, but it does not adjust for the slightly different number of each weekday in the calendar or show year-to-year shifts.

options.metric: Average police-reported crashes per calendar occurrence of each weekday
options.denominator: Calendar days of each weekday from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (678 or 679 days, depending on weekday)
options.grouping: Day of week across the full period
options.reason: A per-day average controls for the small difference in how often each weekday occurs in the 13-year interval.
options.answer: Friday averaged 499.7 crashes per calendar day, the highest, while Sunday averaged 379.9, the lowest.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the typical calendar-day crash volume for each weekday, with Friday highest (499.7) and Sunday lowest (379.9). Dividing by the number of weekday occurrences is defensible because this interval has 678 or 679 of each weekday; the pooled average still leaves year-to-year changes unanswered.
